title: Machine learning and cell assays implicate sphinganine-1-phosphate in paclitaxel-induced neuropathy
summary: Lipidomics of 255 lipid mediators in blood of 31 breast cancer patients before and after paclitaxel was analysed with supervised machine learning, which found 27 lipids that classified pre- versus post-therapy samples with a median balanced accuracy of up to 90%. The top hit, sphinganine-1-phosphate (SA1P), induced calcium transients in sensory neurons via TRPV1 and sphingosine-1-phosphate receptors and differed between patients with and without neuropathy. The cohort is small and the neuropathy link is preliminary.
ai_technology: Supervised machine-learning classifiers with feature selection on blood lipid mediators
organization: Goethe University Frankfurt; Fraunhofer Institute for Translational Medicine and Pharmacology

evidence.tested: Held-out validation subset before feature selection; calcium imaging of SA1P in sensory neurons.
evidence.unknown: Whether SA1P contributes to neuropathy in patients; specific algorithms were not confirmed in the reviewed material.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning feature selection pointed to SA1P among 27 paclitaxel-regulated lipids.
